title: Scale-Shift and Fractional Fourier Transform as Rotations over Finite Holographic Substrate

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The framed substrate: the Subject $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$ with $\p=4\kap+1$, its register $\pi=2\kap$, $\im=-\gen^{\kap}=\gen^{-\kap}$, $e=\gen^{\im}$; the frame-relative labels and the atlas of presentations $\gen\mapsto\gen^{u}$; time as scale-dilation, the generator as the observer's own advance.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: The Weil representation $\omega_\p$ of $\SL(2,\Fp)$ and its Schr\"odinger model, the finite Fourier transform representing the rotation $w$, the finite harmonic oscillator; the scalar convention $\omega_\p(w)^{2}=\omega_\p(-I)$, $\omega_\p(w)^{4}=I$.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: The classical evaluation of the twisted quadratic Gauss sum for $4\mid n$, $\sum_k\zeta_n^{uk^{2}}=\bigl(\tfrac{\kap}{u}\bigr)(1\pm i)\sqrt n$; the eigenvalue quartet of prime-modulus number-theoretic transforms; the multiplicity counts of the discrete Fourier eigenvalues; the Gauss sign through the Weil representation.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The entropic uncertainty relation for a pair of bases, $H_{B}+H_{B'}\ge-2\log c$, $c$ the maximal overlap, $c=n^{-1/2}$ for mutually unbiased bases, saturated by basis-localized states.

rows.label: A5
rows.predicate: The framed-rational zoom: the grids $G_n$ and their $(\p-1)$-periodicity $G_{n+(\p-1)}=G_n$, the meridian shift $m\mapsto m-1$ as the refinement step.

rows.label: A6
rows.predicate: The measurement layer: probabilities are structural weights of the cyclotomic stratum, the finite-field module carries no Born magnitude, and the readout is an observer-side declaration; the shell dynamics a bijection, entropy attaching to the readout.

rows.label: A7
rows.predicate: The continuum fractional Fourier transform and the finite constructions the family is placed against: the eigenbasis transforms, the eigenvector-free and matrix-function transforms, the canonical DFT eigenbasis, the arithmetic FrFT of the rotation group, the harmonic-oscillator propagator reading.

rows.label: A8
rows.predicate: The framework's reading of the holographic principle: the capacity $\dS$ of the totality as the count and the entropy, the area law $A=4\dS$ read exactly as $A=\Om-1$, the origin the one point no boundary chart registers; the totality a finite holographic substrate when the observer's label plane $\Fp\times\Fp$ fits inside its count, $\p^{2}<\Om$; every substrate-anchored measure as boundary data.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.euler_identity
B2.doc: 2:D6, 6:B2, 00:C14 — the Euler identity on the shell: with `e = g^i` and `π = 2κ`, `(g^i)^{i·2κ} = (−1)^i` for every natural reading `i` of the quarter-turn — `−1` exactly when `i` is odd.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orientation_class
B3.doc: 2:D5, 6:B3, 13:B2 — the orientation classes: for `g' = g^u`, the quarter-turn `−g'^κ` is `−g^κ` when `u ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `−(−g^κ)` when `u ≡ 3 (mod 4)`.

B5.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_relations
B5.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 — every shell: on a field with `p = 4κ + 1` elements, `n = p − 1`, `g` a primitive root and `F = i • W`: `W² = −J`, `F² = J`, `F⁴ = 1`, `W J = J W`.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.F_sq
B5.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 (`F² = J`, entrywise): the quarter-turn transform squares to the reversal.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.J_sq
B5.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 (`J² = 1`, entrywise): the reversal is an involution, so `F⁴ = J² = 1`.

B6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.ofNat_n
B6.doc: 6:B6 — the normalization constant read in the field: `n = p − 1 ≡ −1`.

B6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.sqrt_neg_one
B6.doc: 6:B6, the square roots of `−1 = 1/n` in the field are exactly `±i`.

B6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.scaled_W_sq_iff
B6.doc: 6:B6, `(c W)² = J` exactly when `c = ±i`: `(cW)² = c² W² = −c² J`.

B7.name: FRC.Fourier.shell_relations
B7.doc: 6:B5, 6:B7 — every shell: on a field with `p = 4κ + 1` elements, `n = p − 1`, `g` a primitive root and `F = i • W`: `W² = −J`, `F² = J`, `F⁴ = 1`, `W J = J W`.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.symm_antisymm_decomp
B7.doc: 6:B7 — the decomposition `V = V⁺ ⊕ V⁻`: with `h = 2⁻¹`, `v = v⁺ + v⁻` where `v⁺ k = h(v k + v (rev k))` is symmetric and `v⁻ k = h(v k − v (rev k))` antisymmetric; the decomposition is unique.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.symm_antisymm_unique
B7.doc: 6:B7 — the decomposition is unique: a vector that is both symmetric and antisymmetric is zero, so the symmetric and antisymmetric parts of `v` are determined.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.symm_determined
B7.doc: 6:B7 — a symmetric vector is determined by its `2κ + 1` coordinates `v 0, …, v (2κ)`.

B7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.antisymm_determined
B7.doc: 6:B7 — an antisymmetric vector is determined by its `2κ − 1` coordinates `v 1, …, v (2κ − 1)`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.proj_mul_self
C2.doc: 6:C2, the idempotence: `Π_ℓ Π_ℓ = Π_ℓ`, the four coefficients `q² Σ u^a u^{r−a} = q u^r` with `u⁴ = 1`, `4q = 1`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.proj_mul_ne
C2.doc: 6:C2, the orthogonality: `Π_ℓ Π_m = 0` for `ℓ ≠ m` below 4, each coefficient `q² v^r (1 + x + x² + x³)` with `x = u v³` a nontrivial fourth root of unity.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.sum_proj
C2.doc: 6:C2, the resolution of the identity: `Π₀ + Π₁ + Π₂ + Π₃ = I`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Fmat_proj
C2.doc: 6:C2, the eigen-relation: `F Π_ℓ = i^ℓ Π_ℓ`, the coefficients of `F Π_ℓ` the cyclic shift of `Π_ℓ`'s and `i^ℓ = u³` with `u = w^ℓ`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_add
C3.doc: 6:C3, additivity: `F^{[s+r]} = F^{[s]} F^{[r]}` on the cycle, a representation of `ℤ/(p−1)`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_cardinal
C3.doc: 6:C3, the cardinal values: `F^{[0]} = I`, `F^{[κ]} = F`, `F^{[2κ]} = J`, `F^{[3κ]} = F J`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_period
C3.doc: 6:C3, the period: the family is periodic over the cycle, `F^{[s + (p−1)]} = F^{[s]}`, so `F^{[4κ]} = I`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_pow
C3.doc: 6:C3, the root: `F^{[m s]} = (F^{[s]})^m`; in particular `(F^{[1]})^κ = F^{[κ]} = F`.

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_injective
C4.doc: 6:C4, 6:D2, faithfulness: `F^{[s]} = F^{[r]}` entrywise forces `s = r` below the period, for `κ ≥ 2`. The entry `(2, 1)` of `F^{[s]} Π₁ = z^s Π₁` reads `z^s (Π₁)₂₁` with `(Π₁)₂₁ ≠ 0`, so `z^s = z^r` and `z` has order `4κ`.

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_frames
C4.doc: 6:C4, 6:C5, 6:D2, the shell `p = 5` has exactly the two frames `g = 2` and `g = 3`.

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_faithful
C4.doc: 6:C4, 6:D2, faithfulness at `p = 5` on both frames (`z = g⁻¹`: `3` for `g = 2`, `2` for `g = 3`).

C4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_odd_proj
C4.doc: 6:C5, 6:C4, at `p = 5` exactly one odd projector vanishes: `Π₁ = 0 ≠ Π₃` at `g = 2`, `Π₃ = 0 ≠ Π₁` at `g = 3`; the surviving odd projector carries the faithful character `s ↦ z^{ms}`, `m` its index.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.proj_even_sum
C5.doc: 6:C5, the even sum: `Π₀ + Π₂ = (q + q)(I + J)`, with `q + q = 2⁻¹` (`half`).

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.proj_odd_sum
C5.doc: 6:C5, the odd sum: `Π₁ + Π₃ = (q + q)(I − J)`.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.even_proj_ne_zero
C5.doc: 6:C5, the even projectors never vanish: `(Π₀)₀₀ ≠ 0` and `(Π₂)₀₀ ≠ 0` on every frame, since `q + q = 2⁻¹` and `1 ± i` are nonzero.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.odd_proj_ne_zero
C5.doc: 6:C5, the odd projectors do not vanish for `κ ≥ 2`: the entry `(2, 1)` of each is `±q (g² − g^{−2}) ≠ 0`.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_frames
C5.doc: 6:C4, 6:C5, 6:D2, the shell `p = 5` has exactly the two frames `g = 2` and `g = 3`.

C5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_odd_proj
C5.doc: 6:C5, 6:C4, at `p = 5` exactly one odd projector vanishes: `Π₁ = 0 ≠ Π₃` at `g = 2`, `Π₃ = 0 ≠ Π₁` at `g = 3`; the surviving odd projector carries the faithful character `s ↦ z^{ms}`, `m` its index.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.trace_powers
C7.doc: 6:C7, the traces of the cardinal powers: `Tr I = −1`, `Tr F = i G`, `Tr F² = Tr J = 2`, `Tr F³ = Tr FJ = i Ḡ`.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.trace_proj
C7.doc: 6:C7, the trace of a projector in trace form: `Tr Π_ℓ = q (Tr I + u Tr F + u² Tr J + u³ Tr FJ)`, `u = w^ℓ`, i.e. `Tr Π_ℓ = ¼ Σ_r i^{−ℓr} Tr F^r`.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.gauss_mul
C7.doc: 6:C7, `G Ḡ = −2`: the substitution `k = l + d` and the geometric sum over `l`.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.gauss_conj
C7.doc: 6:C7, the conjugate law: when `G = ε (1 + i)` with `ε² = 1`, the conjugate frame's Gauss sum is `Ḡ = −ε (1 − i)`, i.e. `ε(g⁻¹) = −ε(g)`.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.trace_tuples
C7.doc: 6:C7, the dichotomy: under `G = ε (1 + i)` the traces of the projectors are `(κ, κ, κ+1, κ−1)` for `ε = 1` and `(κ+1, κ−1, κ, κ)` for `ε = −1`, read in the field.

C7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.six_tuples
C7.doc: 6:C7, the tuples on the six shells: `(2, 0, 1, 1)` at `p = 5` (`ε = −1`) and `(κ, κ, κ+1, κ−1)` at the five others.

C8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.lift_add
C8.doc: 6:C8, every lift is additive: `U^{(a)}_{s+r} = U^{(a)}_s U^{(a)}_r`, by the projector algebra alone.

C8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.lift_cardinal
C8.doc: 6:C8, the cardinal skeleton: with `a_ℓ ≡ ℓ (mod 4)` the lift agrees with the family at the multiples of `κ`, `U^{(a)}_{mκ} = F^{[mκ]} = F^m` (`frft_pow`, `frft_cardinal`), since `z^{mκ} = i^m` is a fourth root of unity.

C8.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.lift_pow
C8.doc: 6:C8, the lift at the multiples of `κ` is the power of the transform: `U^{(a)}_{mκ} = F^m`.

C9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.inv_frame
C9.doc: 6:C9, the conjugate frame: the inverse drive `g⁻¹` is a frame of the same shell and capacity.

C9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Fmat_conj
C9.doc: The conjugate frame's transform is `−F J = −F⁻¹` (6:C9).

C9.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.proj_conj
C9.doc: The conjugate frame's projectors are the shifted ones, `Π'_ℓ = Π_{ℓ+2}` (6:C9).

D1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_inverse
D1.doc: 6:D1, every `F^{[s]}` is invertible: `F^{[s]} F^{[n−s]} = I = F^{[n−s]} F^{[s]}` for `s ≤ n = p − 1`.

D2.name: FRC.Fourier.mul_J_apply
D2.doc: 6:D2 — `J` is a permutation matrix: `(M J) k j = M k (−j)`, so `M J` has the columns of `M`, reindexed by the parity involution `j ↦ −j`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_injective
D2.doc: 6:C4, 6:D2, faithfulness: `F^{[s]} = F^{[r]}` entrywise forces `s = r` below the period, for `κ ≥ 2`. The entry `(2, 1)` of `F^{[s]} Π₁ = z^s Π₁` reads `z^s (Π₁)₂₁` with `(Π₁)₂₁ ≠ 0`, so `z^s = z^r` and `z` has order `4κ`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_frames
D2.doc: 6:C4, 6:C5, 6:D2, the shell `p = 5` has exactly the two frames `g = 2` and `g = 3`.

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.five_faithful
D2.doc: 6:C4, 6:D2, faithfulness at `p = 5` on both frames (`z = g⁻¹`: `3` for `g = 2`, `2` for `g = 3`).

D2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_half_turn
D2.doc: 6:D2, the half-turn is the reversal: `F^{[s + 2κ]} = F^{[s]} J`, entrywise `F^{[s+2κ]}_{kj} = F^{[s]}_{k, rev j}`, so the framed bases `B_{s+2κ}` and `B_s` agree as unordered bases.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.meridian_scale
D4.doc: 6:D4 — meridian-scale covariance: `S_r(M_m) = M_{m+r}` as ordered lists, for every `m, r`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.meridian_step
D4.doc: 6:D4 — the effective step: consecutive entries of `M_m` differ by `g^m`, `(a + 1) g^m = a g^m + g^m`.

D4.name: FRC.Shell.scale_periodic
D4.doc: 6:D4 — `S_{r + (p−1)} = S_r`: the meridian-scale map is `(p − 1)`-periodic in `r` (the periodicity of the framed-rational zoom, A5).

D5.name: FRC.Shell.ladder13
D5.doc: 6:D5 — the `p = 13`, `g = 2`, `κ = 3` ladder: `M_0, M_1, M_2, M_3` at the effective steps `1, 2, 4, 8`; `M_0` and `M_1` are unwrapped (`π g^r = 6 g^r < 13` for `r ≤ 1`), `M_2` wraps (`6 · 4 = 24 ≥ 13`: its entries `0, 4, 8, 12, 3, 7, 11` return through the seam).

D7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_row_zero
D7.doc: 6:D7, the row-0 entries of `F^{[t]}` off the site `j = 0`: `F^{[t]}_{0j} = (q + q)(1 − z^{2t}) i = (i/2)(1 − g^{−2t})`, the same value at every `0 < j < n`.

D7.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.frft_row_zero_ne_zero
D7.doc: 6:D7, the row-0 entries off the site are nonzero for `t ∉ {0, 2κ}` (the paper reads: `F^{[t]}` is not monomial, `B_{s+t} ≠ B_s`, exactly `2κ` measurement bases).

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.rot_circle
E2.doc: 6:E2, `R_s ∈ SO(2, 𝔽_p)`: `c_s² + d_s² = 1` (the determinant), since `z_s z_s⁻¹ = 1`.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.rot_hom
E2.doc: 6:E2, `s ↦ R_s` is a homomorphism: `R_{s+r} = R_s R_r` entrywise.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.rot_inj
E2.doc: 6:E2, injectivity below the period: `R_s = R_r` forces `s = r`, since `c + i d = z^s` and `z` has order `4κ`.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.rot_surj
E2.doc: 6:E2, surjectivity: every point of the circle `c² + d² = 1` is a rotation `R_s`, `s < 4κ`: `c + i d ≠ 0` is a power `z^s` of the generator, and then `c = c_s`, `d = d_s`.

E2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.six_circles
E2.doc: 6:E2, 6:E10, the circle has `4κ` points on the six shells: `4, 12, 16, 28, 36, 40`.

C6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.Fmat_chart
C6.doc: 6:C6, the chart `g^{u²}` of an odd `u` is the coordinate relabelling `m ↦ um`: `F(g^{u²})_{kj} = F(g)_{uk, uj}`, the indices read mod `n`; the quarter-turn is unchanged since `u² ≡ 1 (mod 4)`.

C6.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.thirteen_tuples
C6.doc: 6:C6, the two frames `g = 2` and `g = 6` of `p = 13`: the traces of the projectors read `(3, 3, 4, 2)` and `(4, 2, 3, 3)`, the multiplicity tuples, and `Tr F = 4, 9`.

C11.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.W_chart
C11.doc: 6:C11, the chart's Fourier matrix is the relabelled one: `W(g^u)_{kj} = W(g)_{k, uj}`, the index read mod `n` (`W(g^u) = W P_u`).

C11.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.W_mul_chart
C11.doc: 6:C11, `W · W(g^u) = −J P_u`: entrywise `−[k + uj ≡ 0 (mod n)]`, by the geometric sum.

C11.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.chart_noncommute
C11.doc: 6:C11, the non-commutation: when `u² ≢ 1 (mod n)` the entry `(−u, 1)` of `W · W(g^u)` is `−1` and that of `W(g^u) · W` is `0`, so the chart `g^u` does not commute with the frame's `W`.

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.rot_uv
E10.doc: 6:E10, the rotation on the plane in the coordinates `u = x + i y`, `v = x − i y`: `R_s` scales `u` by `z_s` and `v` by `z_s⁻¹`.

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.orbit_free
E10.doc: 6:E10, the orbits off the origin are free: a rotation `R_s`, `s < 4κ`, fixing a point `(x, y) ≠ (0, 0)` is the identity, `s = 0`.

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.plane_count
E10.doc: 6:E10, the count `p² = 1 + (4κ + 2) · 4κ` (the paper reads it as the origin and `4κ + 2` free orbits of size `4κ`).

E10.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.six_circles
E10.doc: 6:E2, 6:E10, the circle has `4κ` points on the six shells: `4, 12, 16, 28, 36, 40`.
